### 1 of 1. 1 name in the profile reply in src/api/profile.ts breaks the naming rule

### What was found
The profile reply sends a value to outside programs under a name written as `displayName` at src/api/profile.ts line 18: `return { displayName: profile.name };`. No other card covers this file.

### Why it matters
The project's rule is that names in the data the service sends to outside programs use lowercase words joined by underscores, so this one should be `display_name`. The rule comes from AGENTS.md, in its API naming section.

### What happens if you accept
A fix would rename `displayName` to `display_name` in that reply. Programs that already read `displayName` would stop finding it, so this cleanup cannot make that change. A ticket would record the item for a planned change and leave the code as it is now. You approve the ticket's exact text separately before it is filed.

Pick one:
1. [ ] Fix - unavailable: renaming it would break existing programs that read `displayName`
2. [ ] Ticket - file one ticket listing them and change nothing now [recommended]
3. [ ] Ignore - leave them as they are

### 1 of 1. One public response field in src/api/profile.ts uses the wrong name

### What was found
At `src/api/profile.ts:18`, `return { displayName: profile.name };` uses `displayName` instead of `display_name`. No other class shares this file.

### Why it matters
The API naming rule in `AGENTS.md` requires public JSON response fields to use lowercase words separated by underscores. Existing clients consume `displayName`, so renaming it would change the public contract. Fix is unavailable under this run’s safety limits.

### What happens if you accept
The proposed change replaces `displayName` with `display_name`. Choosing Ticket prepares one ticket describing the mismatch and compatibility concern, leaving the code unchanged. Filing requires separate approval of the ticket’s exact text.

Pick one:
1. [ ] Fix - unavailable: renaming this field changes the public API contract.
2. [ ] Ticket [recommended] - file one ticket listing the finding and change nothing now.
3. [ ] Ignore - leave it as it is.

The empty `[ ]` boxes with `[recommended]` as a bare label keep the card unanswered, and "You approve the ticket's exact text separately before it is filed" makes clear nothing has been filed.
